DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph FEB 07 2020 DILG OPINION NO. S. HONORABLE MEMBERS OF THE SANGGUNIANG BAYAN Anahawan, Southern Leyte Thru: HON. NESTOR B. VESTAL Vice-mayor/Presiding Officer Ladies/Gentlemen : This refers to your Resolution No. 218, series of 2019 entitled "RESOLUTION DECLARING THE NEWLY FORMALLY INSTALLED MUNICIPAL MAYOR ROBERTO A. LOQUINTE AS 'PERSONA NON GRATA' OF THE MUNICIPALITY OF ANAHAWAN," a copy of which was recently received by the Department. The term "persona non grata" is a Latin phrase which means "an unwelcome person". Such practice of declaring a person as persona non grata is enshrined in the 1961 Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations. A diplomat who is no longer welcome to the government to which he is accredited is barred from remaining in the country and declared as persona non grata. In the country, our local sanggunians tend to imitate such practice and thus issue resolutions declaring several persons as persona non grata. To name a few, in 2018, the Sangguniang Panlungsod of Davao City passed a Resolution declaring Senator Antonio Trillanes IV as persona non grata over his remarks that the city was "the most dangerous city in the Philippines"l. Of recent, the Sangguniang Panlungsod of the City of Manila passed a resolution declaring militant group 'Panday Sining' as persona non grata in the nation's capita12. It is settled that there are two (2) outputs that may be generated by our local sanggunians, namely, (1) an ordinance, or (2) a resolution. In the case of the Municipality of Paranaque vs. V.M. Realty Corporation3, the Supreme Court has exhaustively differentiated an ordinance from a resolution, thus: We are not convinced by petitioner's insistence that the terms "resolution " and "ordinance" are synonymous. A municipal ordinance is different from a resolution. An ordinance is a law, but a resolution is merely a declaration of the sentiment or opinion of a lawmaking body on a specific matter. An ordinance possesses a general and permanent character, but a resolution is temporary in nature. Additionally, the two are enacted differently — a third reading is necessary for an ordinance, but not for a resolution, unless decided otherwise by a majority of all the Sanggunian members. No. 127820, 20 July 1998.

Based on the foregoing, a resolution is merely a declaration of the sentiment or opinion of a lawmaking body on a specific matter. Thus, a resolution declaring a certain person as persona non grata is a declaration of the sentiment of a lawmaking body over that person. Applying this in the case of Resolution No. 218, series of 2019 you passed, such piece of legislation is merely a declaration of your sentiment over Mayor Roberto Loquinte, who,you're your perception, is not the right person to govern their municipality. While it is true however that a local sanggunian like you may pass a resolution declaring your sentiment and that would include declaring a certain person as persona non grata, the same must be done within the bounds of law. That is, if such declaration is your way of expressing your sentiment, this is perfectly within your authority. However, if such declaration would already engender preventing Mayor Loquinte from assuming his office and/or discharging his functions, this is already reprehensible. Thus, you are hereby advised to act within the bounds of law and abide by the duly-issued COMELEC Writ of Execution. Until such time that the writ of execution is reversed by a competent court, the same remains valid and must be enforced. Dura lex, sed lex. The law may be hard to observe or difficult to obey, but it remains the law and must be therefore followed just the same. Please be guided accordingly. Very y yo s, . ARAYAN 09167058980/09169805163 Gentlemen/Ladies: This refers to your undated letter furnishing the Department a copy of your letter to President Rodrigo Roa Duterte regarding the political crisis that is presently hounding the Municipality of Anahawan, Southern Leyte which was brought about by the issuance of the Commission on Elections (COMELEC) of a Writ of Execution in favor of Roberto Loquinte. Undersigned understands your predicament. However, there being a duly-issued COMELEC Writ of Execution in favor of Mayor Roberto Loquinte, the same remains valid and must be enforced. Dura lex, sed lex. The law may be hard to observe or difficult to obey, but it remains the law and must be therefore followed just the same. In this regard, you are hereby advised to act within the bounds of law and abide by the duly-issued COMELEC Writ of Execution, until such time that it is reversed by a competent court. Thank you.
